correctness.rationale: The explicit 24-point integer coordinates and five orthogonal generators have 1152 verified distinct induced permutations. Every group map preserves all 276 squared vertex pairs. The checker enumerates all 42,504 unordered five-subsets, partitions them into 81 disjoint generated orbits, verifies 81 distinct canonical ten-pair distance signatures, and checks equality between the complete intrinsic metric automorphism group and the restrictions of each orbit representative set stabilizer. This surjectivity, together with signatures and conjugacy, proves every prescribed five-subset distance isometry extends globally. All 81 classes have exact determinant, size and representative data in the attached TSV; an independent Burnside coefficient sum is 93,312/1,152=81. The verifier accounts for nontrivial pointwise stabilizer kernels of dependent configurations. All arithmetic is exact; the proof is finite and exhaustive, not statistical.

value.rationale: Five points are the natural cardinality of four-dimensional vertex-supported simplices. The result establishes a non-obvious local-to-global metric rigidity principle for *specified* maps on arbitrary five-vertex subsets of the exceptional regular 24-cell and fully classifies all 81 congruence types, including 32 degenerate types. Prior determinant counts and regular flag transitivity cannot resolve this finer symmetry-reduction question. The exact profiles provide complete normal forms for future geometric invariants of five-vertex configurations, without requiring a wider theorem.
